messages.content: 在壓力為10千帕的情況下，水的凝固點是多少？

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
**Answer**

At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 MPa), the freezing point of pure water is essentially the same as at standard atmospheric pressure. Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice–water transition (dT/dP ≈ −0.0075 K MPa⁻¹ for ice Ih), the shift from 101.3 kPa to 10 kPa is:

\[
\Delta T \approx \frac{dT}{dP}\,\Delta P
          \approx (-0.0075\,\text{K MPa}^{-1})(0.0913\,\text{MPa})
          \approx -0.0007\,\text{K}
\]

So the melting/freezing temperature drops by only about **0.001 °C**, giving a freezing point of roughly **0 °C** (more precisely –0.001 °C).

---

**Why I didn’t call the function**

The available `thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point` function only computes boiling points; it does not provide freezing points. Therefore, I calculated the freezing point manually using the known slope of the ice–water phase boundary.
